turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): afternoon. sleeve up, we'll check your blood pressure before the doctor sees you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): ok.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): hold still. one eighteen over seventy four, pulse seventy two. that's fine, in you go.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): hey. eish, that queue was long, sorry. i'm doctor naidoo. what's brought you today?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): contraception.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): right. have you used a method before, or is this from scratch?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): pill.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): which one? the name on the box.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): yaz.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): yaz, ja, the combined tablet. you still taking it?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): stopped.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): what made you stop?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): headaches.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): were they bad, and are they still coming, or did they go when you stopped?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): bad. gone.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): with those headaches, any flashing lights, zigzags, blind spots?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): was it one a day, for contraception? how long were you on it, and when did you stop?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): daily. for contraception. two years. last year.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): any operations?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): and do you yourself have diabetes, high blood pressure, or a diagnosed migraine?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): did a clinic ever do a sugar test, or cholesterol, on you?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): last year. sugar. they said it was borderline. no number.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): ok, borderline without a number isn't a diagnosis, we'll leave it. any chest pain?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): calf pain, or swelling in a leg?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): what about your tummy and your bladder, any trouble there?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): periods heavy?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): do you smoke?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): sometimes. weekends.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): family side. sugar, pressure, clots, anyone?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): uh my father had diabetes in his fifties, my mother did not, and another sister has pressure but no sugar.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): ok, so your mom didn't have the diabetes. any tablets in the house that aren't yours? i don't want them landing on your list by mistake.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): sister's bioten. husband's metforman, for his sugar. not mine.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): biotin is your sister's, metformin is your husband's for his sugar. not yours. now, job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol, in your own words.

[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): i'm a cashier at checkers. my hours are eight till five, monday to saturday. diet is pap and veg most nights, takeaways on a friday. exercise, i just walk to the taxi rank. alcohol, a cider on saturdays.

[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): let me think this through out loud. those headaches came on the yaz and left when you stopped, so my working impression is they were from the oestrogen. weekend smoking on top, even if it's not daily, and i wouldn't restart a combined pill. not a firm diagnosis, just where i'm leaning.

[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): so, err, the options that make more sense. a progestogen only pill, the injection every eight weeks, no, sorry, every twelve weeks, or a coil, or the implant. implanon sits in the arm for three years, no oestrogen, very effective, though the bleeding can be all over the show. you don't have to choose today.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): implant.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): leaning to the implant, ja. we'll give you the leaflet and see you back to decide properly. nothing to start tonight.
[SEG0048] person_1 (NURSE): printer's down again, but i've got a paper copy. here's the implanon leaflet. i've booked her back in 2 weeks, thursday morning.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): read that leaflet before you come, and if you can skip those weekend cigarettes it keeps more doors open. see you in two weeks.

spec.situation: Young woman asks about contraception, previous pill caused headaches, smokes occasionally; blood pressure read; options discussed; implant leaflet given, decision next visit.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

bad.reason: Husband's diabetes is mentioned, but as his condition, not patient family history asked here.
Follow-up in 2 weeks is supported; planned by nurse/clinic, not specifically doctor.
